newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hotel rooms galore for historic Hong Kong bash.
newsitem.headline: Hotel rooms galore for historic Hong Kong bash.

text.p: Hoteliers said on Tuesday there were rooms galore in Hong Kong for travellers keen to witness the territory's reversion to Chinese rule, despite predictions that all hotel rooms would be reserved months in advance.
Britain hands back its colony of more than 150 years to China at midnight on June 30.
Calling Hong Kong's handover party the bash of the year, pundits had predicted hotel rooms would be impossible to find for tourists who wanted to see the celebrations and handover ceremonies.
"This is simply not true -- there are still rooms available for booking in Hong Kong hotels," the Hong Kong Hotels Association (HKHA) said in a special handover newsletter.

There were 7,000 rooms in hotels listed with the HKHA available as of Tuesday, including many at "the low end of the price range" for dates around July 1, an HKHA official said. The HKHA lists 92 hotels with a total of 35,000 rooms.
A Hong Kong legislator said hotel operators had only themselves to blame because they had jacked up prices around the handover in anticipation of a rise in demand.

"Too many hotels presumed they were going to be full and became greedy. Now they have ended up shooting themselves in the foot," legislator Howard Young was quoted as saying in the South China Morning Post.
Some five-star hotels have pushed up prices for rooms around the time of the handover by more than 60 percent.
